questions.text:
Ocean acidification occurs due to carbon dioxide in the atmosphere dissolving into seawater and forming various acids.

One step of this process is shown below:

H₂CO₃(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ HCO₃⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)    Kc = 4.30 x 10⁻⁷

Write the equilibrium constant expression for this reaction.
questions.expectedAnswer: Kc = [HCO₃⁻][H₃O⁺] / [H₂CO₃]
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct Kc expression.

questions.text:
The value of the equilibrium constant is 4.30 x 10⁻⁷.

Explain what this indicates about the ratio of products and reactants.
questions.expectedAnswer: Kc is the concentration of products divided by the concentration of reactants.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: A correct statement about the magnitude of Kc OR the method of calculating Kc. Merit: Explains the ratio of products to reactants AND identifies that the reaction must favour reactants/reverse reaction.

questions.text:
Global oceanic temperatures have been increasing since the industrial revolution.

Predict the impact on the position of equilibrium as temperature increases, if the enthalpy of this reaction is ΔrH = -3.85 kJ mol⁻¹.

In your answer:
- describe the effect of temperature on the forward and reverse reactions
- explain any changes that would occur to the value of Kc.

You do not need to perform any calculations.
questions.expectedAnswer: The enthalpy of the reaction is a negative value, showing the forward reaction is exothermic
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that increasing temperature will favour the endothermic reaction OR identifies that Kc will be affected by temperature OR identifies that more products are being made. Merit: Identifies that the reverse reaction is favoured to absorb the added heat/minimise the change OR explains that the Kc decrease shows reactants favoured when temp is increased. Excellence: Fully describes the effect of temperature on the forward and reverse reactions, and explains the change in Kc linked to more products being produced.

questions.text: Calculate the pH of a 0.25 mol L⁻¹ solution of hydrochloric acid, HCl.
questions.expectedAnswer:
pH = -log₁₀[H₃O⁺]
pH = -log₁₀(0.25)
pH = 0.602
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct value.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of hydroxide ions, OH⁻, in a solution of hydrochloric acid, HCl, with a pH of 1.3.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One step correct. Merit: Correct answer with correct units and 2-4 s.f. (use of pOH is acceptable).

questions.text:
Compare the pH and conductivity of hydrochloric acid, HCl, and carbonic acid, H₂CO₃.

| | Hydrochloric Acid, HCl | Carbonic Acid, H₂CO₃ |
|---|---|---|
| Acid Strength | Strong | Weak |
| pH | 1.0 | 4.7 |
| Concentration | 0.10 mol L⁻¹ | 0.10 mol L⁻¹ |

In your answer, include:
- definitions for strong and weak acids
- an explanation of the pH for each solution (HCl and H₂CO₃) and relevant equations
- a definition of conductivity
- an explanation for the conductivity of each solution (HCl and H₂CO₃).
questions.expectedAnswer: Weak acids dissociate partially in water, while strong acids dissociate completely into their...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that strong acids completely dissociate, while weak acids partially dissociate OR defines pH OR defines conductivity. Merit: Explains the pH in relation to dissociation for both solutions AND explains the conductivity of both solutions in relation to dissociation. Excellence: Justifies both properties (pH and conductivity) relative to each other with explanation and relevant equations.

questions.text:
Paua are a species of marine organism, which form their shells from layers of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, and proteins. This layering leads to a very strong shell structure with a dull, pitted outer layer and smooth, shiny inner layer. Unfortunately, the calcium carbonate reacts with acid in the oceans leading to degradation of their shells.

Describe the chemical observations made when the calcium carbonate shells react with acid in the ocean.
questions.expectedAnswer: The shells will slowly lose mass (become thinner), and bubbles will form
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that mass/thickness will be lost OR bubbles form OR surface becomes rougher/more pitted.

questions.text:
Cross-sectional views of two different paua shells are shown below.

[Diagram shows two shell cross-sections with outer (surface, dark) and inner (shiny, light) layers marked. Paua Shell A has Total Shell Area = 110 cm². Paua Shell B has Total Shell Area = 220 cm².]

Explain which paua shell is more vulnerable to the effects of ocean acidification.

In your answer, include concepts of:
- collision theory
- rate of reaction.
questions.expectedAnswer: Shell B will be more vulnerable. This is
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies Shell B as having a greater surface area OR identifies rate of reaction increases with surface area. Merit: Full explanation linking surface area to collision theory and rate.

questions.text:
Paua use enzymes like carbonic anhydrase to help form their shells. Enzymes are biomolecules that act as catalysts for specific reactions.

The graph shows the change in the mass of the paua shell over time without the use of an enzyme.

[Graph shows a curve of mass vs time (months) that rises steeply at first then levels off, labelled 'without enzyme']

Add a second line to the graph to predict the change in mass over time when using the enzyme.
questions.expectedAnswer: Second line shows faster rate (above first line), reaching the same final mass sooner
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Second line shows faster rate (above first line).

questions.text:
Discuss how the carbonic anhydrase enzyme affects the rate of the reaction to form paua shell.

In your answer, refer to:
- the role of a catalyst
- collision theory
- activation energy.
questions.expectedAnswer: Catalysts increase the rate of a reaction
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that a catalyst increases rate of reaction OR basic definition of a catalyst (lowers activation energy and provides an alternative pathway). Merit: Links the higher rate of reaction to the lower activation energy requirement and the catalyst providing the alternative pathway. Excellence: Relates alternative pathway to lower activation energy, frequency of successful collision, and rate of reaction.

Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, calcium chloride, CaCl₂, and calcium ethanoate, Ca(CH₃COO)₂, are soluble calcium compounds.

CaCl₂(s) -> Ca²⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq)
Ca(CH₃COO)₂(s) -> Ca²⁺(aq) +...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Two correct equations.

questions.text:
Calcium ethanoate will react further once dissolved.

Write an equation for the reaction of ethanoate, CH₃COO⁻.
questions.expectedAnswer: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that the reaction of ethanoate occurs with water. Merit: Correct equation in (ii), including arrow OR identifies that the reaction of ethanoate occurs with water including a reversible arrow.

questions.text:
The pH of 0.10 mol L⁻¹ solutions of these three compounds is below.

| Solution | Ca(OH)₂ | CaCl₂ | Ca(CH₃COO)₂ |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH | 13.2 | 7 | 8 |

Discuss the differences in their pH.

In your answer:
- give a definition for acids and bases
- explain how proton transfer is linked to pH
- discuss any ability for these compounds to transfer protons.
questions.expectedAnswer: Acids can donate protons, while bases can accept them.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises the nature of TWO of the three solutions OR definition for acid and base. Merit: Explains in (iii) how calcium ethanoate acts as a basic salt OR explains that bases accept protons so hydroxide is a base OR recognises that CaCl₂ fully dissociates and no proton transfer occurs. Excellence: Fully discusses the differences in compound pH by defining acid and base, explaining how proton transfer is linked to pH, and justifying the pH of two compounds including calcium ethanoate.

questions.text:
Phosphorus pentachloride, PCl₅, is a common chlorinating agent in organic chemistry. It is produced as a gas using phosphorus trichloride, PCl₃, and chlorine gas, Cl₂:

PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) ⇌ PCl₅(g)

During the manufacturing process, some of the PCl₅ is removed from the reaction vessel.

Explain, using equilibrium principles, how the system responds to restore equilibrium.

In your answer, refer to each of the species present.
questions.expectedAnswer: Removing the product PCl₅ will result in the equilibrium shifting to offset the change/replace...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward is favoured/products favoured. Merit: Correct explanation.

questions.text:
Explain why producing PCl₅ is favoured when the reaction is transferred to a vessel with a much smaller volume.

In your answer, include:
- a description of the changes occurring
- an explanation of equilibrium principles
- what happens to the position of equilibrium when the pressure is increased.
questions.expectedAnswer: Decreasing the volume of the reaction vessel increases the pressure.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Explains why the pressure has increased OR identifies forward is favoured/products favoured. Merit: Identifies pressure favours fewest moles OR why the forward is favoured. Excellence: Fully explains equilibrium principles of pressure increase, and moles of gas linked to equation, justifying favouring production of PCl₅.

questions.text:
The equilibrium expression for the reaction is shown below.

Kc = [PCl₅] / ([PCl₃][Cl₂])

Calculate the equilibrium constant at 300 degrees C if the concentrations are as follows:
[PCl₅] = 0.016 mol L⁻¹
[Cl₂] = 0.021 mol L⁻¹
[PCl₃] = 0.00013 mol L⁻¹
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct value.

questions.text:
Explain the effect of increasing the concentration of Cl₂ on the equilibrium system AND Kc value.

PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) ⇌ PCl₅(g)
questions.expectedAnswer: The increase in concentration favours the forward reaction
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward is favoured. Merit: Explains no change to Kc.

questions.text:
The reaction is set up under new conditions, with different temperatures to favour the production of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl₅.

| | Condition 1 | Condition 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Temperature | 200 degrees C | 700 degrees C |
| Kc | 49 | 0.023 |
| [PCl₅] | 0.12 mol L⁻¹ | 0.15 mol L⁻¹ |
| [Cl₂] | 0.09 mol L⁻¹ | 0.12 mol L⁻¹ |

Use the Kc values to explain which set of conditions (1 or 2) would increase production of PCl₅.
questions.expectedAnswer: Condition 1 would be better
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies Condition 1. Merit: Explains why Condition 1 is better.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of PCl₃ under each of the new conditions listed in (iii).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One with correct process with minor error. Merit: Two concentrations correct.

questions.text:
Chlorine gas, Cl₂(g), can also be used to produce nitrosyl chloride, NOCl(g), a catalyst and industrial bleaching agent.

Cl₂(g) + 2NO(g) ⇌ 2NOCl(g)

The formation of NOCl(g) is favoured when the temperature is decreased.

Explain why this reaction is performed at 95 degrees C instead of a lower temperature (for example, 25 degrees C).

In your answer:
- identify whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic
- explain any disadvantages of a higher temperature using equilibrium concepts
- explain any advantages of using a higher temperature for a reaction using collision theory and rate of reaction principles.
questions.expectedAnswer: The forward reaction must be exothermic, as increasing the temperature favours exothermic (the...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward reaction as exothermic OR describes particles as moving faster/have more kinetic energy. Merit: Explains how temperature favouring the exothermic reaction causes disadvantage AND explains that the forward reaction is determined/influenced by increasing temperature. Excellence: Full explanation, including the compromise of temperature favouring the exothermic reaction causing a disadvantage in yield, but higher temperature increasing rate through collision theory.
